briefs.title: skill publish partial failure testing
briefs.description: Use skill publish partial failure testing to verify consistency when skill creation succeeds but counters, email, or later side effects fail.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test consistency when the skill insert succeeds but the author's published-skill counter update fails?

outline.heading: What Must Skill Publish Partial Failure Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the committed skill insert, caught author-counter failure, asynchronous email work, and the 201 response as separate observable effects.

outline.heading: How Do You Run Partial Database Write Testing?
outline.coverage: Inject failure after the skill insert and assert exactly which database rows and counters persist.

outline.heading: What Is a Skill Counter Consistency Test?
outline.coverage: Compare the author's skillsPublished value with the actual count of owned skills after success, retry, and counter-update failure.

outline.heading: Drizzle Transaction Failure Test Options
outline.coverage: Compare the current nontransactional contract with atomic insert-plus-counter behavior and test each design explicitly.

outline.heading: How Should a Noncritical Side Effect Failure Behave?
outline.coverage: Verify logging and response behavior for counter and email failures without labeling a documented noncritical effect as a total request failure.

outline.heading: Publish API Consistency Recovery
outline.coverage: Test reconciliation, idempotent retry, and derived counter repair while preventing duplicate skill creation.

outline.heading: Failure Point, Persisted State, and Response Matrix
outline.coverage: Present insert, counter, subscriber query, batch email, and response failure points with committed state and recovery action.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Failure Injection Procedure?
outline.coverage: Mock one side effect at a time, call POST, query authoritative state, assert response and logs, then test recovery.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about transactions, noncritical errors, retries, duplicate slugs, counters, email side effects, and reconciliation.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the chosen consistency contract and direct readers to publication and database testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test publish partial failures
steps: Create an authenticated author fixture with a known published-skill count.
Inject a failure into the author counter update after the skill insert.
Call POST and capture the response plus error log.
Assert the new skill exists and the author counter remains unchanged.
Run the chosen reconciliation or transactional recovery path.
Retry safely and assert no duplicate slug or duplicate skill row is created.

codeExamples.title: Inject failure after skill creation
codeExamples.focus: Exercise the skill insert, caught skillsPublished update failure, and final 201 response.

codeExamples.title: Compare skill rows with author counters
codeExamples.focus: Assert the derived number of owned skills against the stored skillsPublished field.

briefs.cta: Open /how-to-publish, browse QA skills at /skills, and add failure injection before the next release.

briefs.title: Typesense publish index freshness testing
briefs.description: Use Typesense publish index freshness testing to measure when a new Postgres skill becomes searchable and detect missing synchronization work.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test whether a newly published Postgres skill becomes searchable when the publish route contains no visible Typesense indexing step?

outline.heading: What Must Typesense Publish Index Freshness Testing Establish?
outline.coverage: Define the publish commit time, first searchable time, maximum observation window, and failure state without assuming an unproven sync mechanism.

outline.heading: How Do You Run a Postgres Typesense Sync Test?
outline.coverage: Publish a uniquely searchable skill, verify its database row, then poll the actual Typesense query until found or timed out.

outline.heading: Why Is a New Skill Missing from Search?
outline.coverage: Investigate absent indexing calls, asynchronous workers, failed document writes, schema rejection, stale aliases, and query field mismatch.

outline.heading: Search Index Freshness SLA Measurement
outline.coverage: Define a product-owned threshold, capture multiple samples, and report observed delay distributions without inventing a target.

outline.heading: How Do You Build a Publish Indexing Integration Test?
outline.coverage: Use real Postgres and disposable Typesense data, unique tokens, bounded polling, exact cleanup, and independent database assertions.

outline.heading: Database Search Eventual Consistency Cases
outline.coverage: Cover creation, update, deletion, indexing failure, delayed sync, duplicate delivery, and retry behavior as separate contracts.

outline.heading: Publish State, Search State, and Freshness Timing
outline.coverage: Present database status, index status, first-hit delay, final outcome, and diagnostic evidence.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Freshness Procedure in CI?
outline.coverage: Create, commit, poll with backoff, fail with evidence, clean both stores, and retain timing artifacts.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about eventual consistency, polling, sync ownership, direct indexing, schema errors, retries, and cleanup.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: Turn freshness into a measurable contract and direct readers to search testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to measure index freshness after publish
steps: Create a publish payload with a unique token in a query_by field.
Record a monotonic timestamp immediately before the POST request.
Assert the 201 response and verify the row directly in PostgreSQL.
Poll Typesense for the unique token with bounded backoff.
Record the first successful hit or fail with database and index diagnostics.
Delete the test row and index document, then verify cleanup.

codeExamples.title: Publish a uniquely searchable skill
codeExamples.focus: Exercise the Postgres insert and document that the visible route has no Typesense write.

codeExamples.title: Poll the production Typesense search path
codeExamples.focus: Search by a unique name or description token and measure first-hit timing.

codeExamples.title: Validate the indexed document schema
codeExamples.focus: Use skillsSchema to diagnose document rejection or missing fields.

briefs.cta: Browse search testing skills at /skills and define a measured publish-to-search freshness target.

briefs.title: Upstash Redis read outage testing
briefs.description: Use Upstash Redis read outage testing to prove a cache read exception becomes a miss and fresh database data still reaches the endpoint in CI.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you verify a Redis read exception becomes a cache miss and the endpoint still fetches fresh database data?

outline.heading: What Must Upstash Redis Read Outage Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define the caught read error, null miss signal, source fetch, nonfatal write attempt, and endpoint response as one testable chain.

outline.heading: How Do You Build an Upstash Outage Fallback Test?
outline.coverage: Mock Redis GET to reject while keeping the source fetcher observable and assert fresh data is returned.

outline.heading: What Does a Redis GET Error Cache Miss Mean?
outline.coverage: Show that cacheGet catches every read exception and returns null, the same value used for a normal miss.

outline.heading: Cache Read Failure Graceful Degradation
outline.coverage: Test successful source reads, source failures after cache errors, and cache write failures without hiding database errors.

outline.heading: How Do You Verify Database Fallback During Redis Outage?
outline.coverage: Use leaderboard or categories as a real consumer and assert the database query executes exactly once per uncached request.

outline.heading: Fault Injection Upstash Test Design
outline.coverage: Inject timeout, rejection, malformed data, and recovery while avoiding dependency on a production Redis service.

outline.heading: Cache Failure, Source Outcome, and Response Matrix
outline.coverage: Present read and write outcomes, fetcher calls, endpoint status, returned source, and diagnostic expectation.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Redis Outage Procedure?
outline.coverage: Stub GET failure, call the consumer, assert fresh data, test SET failure, restore Redis, and verify the next cache hit.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about fail-open caches, read versus write failures, stale data, source errors, timeouts, retries, and observability.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the cache-as-optimization contract and direct readers to reliability testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to verify Redis read outage fallback
steps: Seed deterministic database data for one cacheGetOrSet consumer.
Stub the Redis GET operation to reject with a controlled error.
Call the endpoint and assert its source query executes once.
Assert the endpoint returns the fresh database result successfully.
Stub the subsequent cache SET to fail and assert the response remains unchanged.
Restore Redis behavior and verify a populated cache prevents the source query.

codeExamples.title: Inject read and write failures into cache helpers
codeExamples.focus: Exercise cacheGet catch behavior and cacheGetOrSet source fallback.

codeExamples.title: Verify a real cached endpoint still responds
codeExamples.focus: Assert the leaderboard database fetch runs and its JSON response survives Redis failure.

briefs.cta: Browse cache and resilience testing skills at /skills and add controlled Redis fault injection.

briefs.title: review average rounding contract testing
briefs.description: Use review average rounding contract testing to verify Postgres AVG values become numeric one-decimal ratings without binary rounding surprises.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test Postgres average values and JavaScript conversion are rounded to exactly one decimal without binary surprises?

outline.heading: What Must Review Average Rounding Contract Testing Prove?
outline.coverage: Define integer source ratings, PostgreSQL AVG output, Number conversion, toFixed(1), parseFloat, and numeric zero fallback.

outline.heading: How Do You Build a Postgres AVG Rounding Test?
outline.coverage: Seed rating combinations with exact integers and calculate independent expected averages before calling the endpoint.

outline.heading: What Does Review Average One Decimal Mean?
outline.coverage: Assert numeric value rather than presentation zeros, because parseFloat converts a fixed string back to a number.

outline.heading: JavaScript toFixed API Contract
outline.coverage: Trace Number, toFixed, and parseFloat with boundary-like decimal values and avoid assuming decimal storage beyond integer inputs.

outline.heading: How Do You Run Rating Aggregate Precision QA?
outline.coverage: Use symmetric and asymmetric rating sets, repeat values, and large row counts while validating count and average together.

outline.heading: Empty Average Fallback Test
outline.coverage: Verify null AVG becomes numeric zero and does not pass through Number, toFixed, or parseFloat as an invalid value.

outline.heading: Rating Set, Raw Average, and API Value Matrix
outline.coverage: Present source ratings, exact fraction, database aggregate, one-decimal string, final JSON number, and expected assertion.

outline.heading: How Do You Implement the Rounding Procedure?
outline.coverage: Seed one rating set at a time, query the database aggregate directly, call GET, and compare independent decimal expectations.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about AVG return types, toFixed strings, parseFloat, trailing zeros, empty sets, precision, and display formatting.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the numeric one-decimal API contract and link to review and database testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test review average rounding
steps: Define rating arrays with independently calculated rational averages.
Seed one array for an isolated skill.
Query PostgreSQL AVG and count directly for diagnostic evidence.
Call the review GET endpoint for the same skill.
Assert totalReviews, numeric type, and the expected one-decimal value.
Repeat with an empty skill and assert numeric zero.

codeExamples.title: Assert the AVG conversion pipeline
codeExamples.focus: Exercise avg, Number, toFixed(1), parseFloat, and null fallback.

codeExamples.title: Seed integer rating combinations
codeExamples.focus: Create deterministic review sets using the non-null integer rating column.

briefs.cta: Browse API and database testing skills at /skills and add exact average fixtures to the review suite.

briefs.title: category response ordering testing
briefs.description: Use category response ordering testing to expose unstable taxonomy arrays when PostgreSQL returns rows without an explicit ORDER BY clause in CI.
briefs.coreQuestion: How do you test stable category array ordering when the database query has no ORDER BY clause?

outline.heading: What Must Category Response Ordering Testing Expose?
outline.coverage: Define that the current select has no ordering guarantee and the grouping loop preserves whatever row order the database supplies.

outline.heading: How Do You Demonstrate Postgres Unordered Category Results?
outline.coverage: Use differing insertion patterns and query plans as evidence, without relying on nondeterminism as the only failing test mechanism.

outline.heading: What Is a Stable Taxonomy Order Test?
outline.coverage: Choose an explicit product order such as name then ID, seed ties, and assert each response group independently.

outline.heading: Category API Flaky Ordering Symptoms
outline.coverage: Trace unstable arrays into snapshots, UI filter order, cache repopulation, and cross-environment differences.

outline.heading: How Do You Catch a Missing ORDER BY Regression?
outline.coverage: Inspect generated SQL or query construction and pair the structural check with behavior fixtures that defeat insertion-order assumptions.

outline.heading: Deterministic Category Arrays
outline.coverage: Compare database ordering before grouping with in-memory sorting after grouping and test the chosen contract for all four arrays.

outline.heading: Fixture Order, Expected Sort, and Group Output
outline.coverage: Present insertion order, names, IDs, type groups, expected order, and actual order.

outline.heading: How Do You Run the Ordering Procedure?
outline.coverage: Seed reverse and tied names, clear cache, call repeatedly, assert explicit order, rebuild cache, and rerun.

outline.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
outline.coverage: Answer questions about SQL ordering guarantees, insertion order, cache effects, locale sorting, ID tiebreakers, and snapshots.

outline.heading: Conclusion
outline.coverage: State the need for an explicit ordering contract and direct readers to taxonomy testing skills.

procedurePlan.heading: How to test deterministic category ordering
steps: Define the expected sort fields and a unique final tiebreaker.
Seed categories in reverse order with duplicate sort values.
Delete the categories:all cache key.
Call the endpoint and assert order inside each of the four groups.
Repopulate the cache and repeat the same response assertion.
Inspect the query or in-memory sort to prove the ordering rule is explicit.

codeExamples.title: Assert ordering after category grouping
codeExamples.focus: Exercise the unordered select, grouping loop, cache population, and proposed explicit order.

codeExamples.title: Seed reverse-order and tied categories
codeExamples.focus: Create names and UUIDs that require a clear primary and final tiebreaker.

briefs.cta: Open /categories, browse QA skills at /skills, and make the taxonomy order an explicit contract.
